html:
The ongoing US-Israel war on Iran remains a central global concern, with reports of extensive damage to US bases in the Gulf from Iranian strikes and warnings from the Pentagon about depleted ammunition and strained supply chains. US President Donald Trump stated the US is nearing the end of the conflict and claims to have engaged in direct talks with Tehran, while the US House of Representatives has voted for a third time to end the war.

US Domestic & Economic: The US Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in three years in a unanimous decision, despite fierce opposition from President Donald Trump, who called it a "hostile" and "political" move and demanded a 1% rate. President Donald Trump also returned to the campaign trail, urging North Carolina voters to "crush the communists" ahead of the November midterms. Elsewhere, the US House voted to hold billionaire Epstein associate Leon Black in contempt of Congress for defying subpoenas related to sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, and President Donald Trump's chief of staff Susie Wiles announced she is cancer-free. The United States also denied Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas a visa to attend next week's UN General Assembly in New York.

Shifting Alliances & Conflicts: Europe moved to strengthen ties with Canada, with the EU chief backing a plan for Canada to become an "associate member," a proposal European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen put forward as President Donald Trump's tariffs drive Ottawa closer to Europe. Trump called this move "laughable" and threatened "serious tariffs" or a halt to trade with the European Union in response. Meanwhile, in Eastern Europe, the US House passed new sanctions targeting Russia as explosions shook Kyiv. Poland reaffirmed its support for Ukraine following recent Russian drone attacks near its border, pledging a "nonprovocative but serious response" to Moscow. Russia is also believed to be tormenting the families of Ukrainian POWs, demanding they help Russia.

Middle East Security & Energy: Leaked photos, provided by active military personnel and obtained by the BBC's partner CBS News, reveal extensive damage at US bases in the Gulf from Iranian strikes, including a severed radar jet, flattened trailers, and wrecked air force planes. Iran's President Pezeshkian expressed readiness to resolve issues with neighbors through diplomacy, while the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) claimed to have downed a US Army MQ-9 drone and Iranian Air Force pilots recounted destroying US helicopters in a surprise raid. Separately, Saudi Arabia condemned Houthi drone attacks targeting Mecca, calling it a "red line," and reported 13 civilians injured in other attacks, with the Houthis denying the Mecca attack. The Saudi Crown Prince met with Egypt's Sisi in Cairo, seeking Egypt's backing as Houthi attacks impact Red Sea oil routes. Additionally, a war-damaged building in Gaza collapsed, killing at least 21 people and leaving dozens missing, and Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun expressed a desire to reach a "security agreement" with Israel.

Global Economy & Markets: Oil prices extended losses, reportedly due to Saudi Arabia offering ship-to-ship crude transfers after a pipeline hit, easing fears of Middle East supply disruptions. However, Brent crude oil reached $105.70 as Gulf states halted Hormuz talks and Saudi Arabia struck Houthis, with shipping through the Strait of Hormuz having sharply plunged. In other financial news, BRICS Pay, a decentralized digital system for international payments in currencies other than the dollar, is being discussed as a potential rival to the West’s SWIFT payments system. Separately, Singapore's 'Fort Knox' is set to auction $2 billion in luxury goods seized by police.

Other Major Developments: Fiji declared a national HIV emergency, with government estimates indicating one in 60 adults in Fiji are now living with HIV, as escalating use of methamphetamine fuels the "epidemic." Encouraging signs have emerged in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola fight, though reports suggest the outbreak may have gone undetected for months. In Europe, Kosovo's ex-President Hashim Thaci was convicted of war crimes and sentenced to 25 years in prison by a European Union-backed court. Australian domestic politics saw Labor back down on plans to impose a $5,000 cap on allied health services for veterans, following weeks of criticism.
